Charts, Reimagined

Prototype gallery for the tally spending report · mock data, Jul 2025 – Jun 2026

Concept 01 · KPI strip

Lead with the numbers, not the chart

The summary cards become a compact stat-tile row: value, signed delta vs the prior 12 months, and a 12-point sparkline. The one ratio (recurring share) is a meter, not a donut.

Concept 02 · Cash flow

Income up, spending down, net on top

The grouped bars become a diverging column chart on one axis: income grows up, spending grows down, and the net line crosses the baseline exactly where the month went red. Only the best and worst months are direct-labeled; hover any month for the full readout.

Concept 03 · Category trend

Stacked, with air between the segments

Top five categories plus “Other”, separated by 2px surface gaps instead of borders. Colors are fixed to the category, so filtering never repaints survivors.

Concept 04 · Category share

The donut becomes a ranked list

Close shares are unreadable on a wheel. A part-to-whole strip keeps the “of the whole” feel; ranked bars below make every comparison exact.

Share of 12-month spending
Concept 05 · Seasonality

Category rhythm heatmap

Where the stacked chart shows totals, the heatmap shows timing: each row is shaded against its own 12-month range (one hue, light→dark), so December’s shopping spike and summer travel pop even next to rent-sized numbers. Hover any cell for the exact amount.

low high · each row relative to its own range
Concept 06 · Follow one category

Emphasis, not eight colors

When the question is “what is Food doing?”, the answer is one accent line against gray context — not a rainbow. Pick a category below; the crosshair reads out every series at the hovered month.

Design rules applied: one axis everywhere · bars ≤24px with 4px rounded data-ends · 2px surface gaps instead of borders · hairline solid gridlines · legends for every multi-series chart, direct labels only where they earn it · color follows the entity, never its rank · text wears text tokens, marks wear the series color.

Generated by tally · prototype, not wired to real data
